In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

That is: begin, or commence, with the naming of Allah, seeking blessing and benediction (tayammun wa tabarruk).

"Allah" is a name that the Creator, glorified is He, has alone; it functions in His description as a proper name does, and no derivation is known for it. It was also said: its meaning is "the One who possesses the worship by which He is intended."

"Ar-Rahman ar-Rahim" are two attributes of Allah, exalted is He, whose meaning is: the Possessor of mercy. That is, mercy is inherent to Him, and it is the will to bestow good. There is no difference between the two, like nadman and nadim (both meaning "companion").
﴿All praise is due to Allah﴾: it is praise of Allah and thanks to Him for His favours. ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾: the Owner of all creatures.

[Qur'an 1:4] ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment.﴾ It is derived from "al-milk" (ownership), and "al-milk" is derived from "al-mulk" (sovereignty); that is, He is the Judge of the Day of Recompense and Reckoning, because He alone holds the decision on that Day.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 1, verse 5:

﴿Iyyāka naʿbudu﴾ meaning: We single You out and direct our worship to You, and ʿibādah is obedience together with humility. ﴿Iyyāka nastaʿīn﴾: And from You we seek help.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 1, verse 6:

﴿Guide us to the straight path.﴾ That is: point us to it, lead us along it, and keep us firm upon it.

ِ﴿The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour﴾ with guidance, and they are the people of Musa and Isa, peace be upon them both, before they changed the blessings of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It has also been said: they are those whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His saying, ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour﴾ [4:69], and so on. ﴿Not of those who have evoked (Your) anger﴾, i.e., not of those upon whom You are angry, and they are the Jews. The meaning of anger from Allah, exalted is He, is the intention of punishment. ﴿Nor of those who are astray﴾, i.e., nor of those who went astray, and they are the Christians. So it is as if the Muslims were asking Allah, exalted is He, to guide them to the path of those upon whom He has bestowed favour, and on whom He has not been angry as He was angry with the Jews, and who did not go astray from the truth as the Christians went astray.
